title: Deputies: Bailey man caught with meth, mushrooms and pot - NewsBreak
text:
By From staff reports ,
7 hours ago
NASHVILLE — Deputies say the Nash County Sheriff’s Office’s new Community Action Team caught a Bailey man with methamphetamine, psilocybin mushrooms and marijuana.
The sheriff’s office conducted a probable-cause search of a home on the 9000 block of Issette Lane near Bailey on Wednesday, May 20, and arrested resident Jesus Ramos-Vargas after finding drugs, Deputy Elizabeth Frisbee said in a news release on Tuesday, May 26.
Deputies seized about 7 grams of methamphetamine, 210 grams (7.4 ounces) of marijuana and 4 grams of psilocybin mushrooms along with a firearm, Frisbee said.
“The marijuana and methamphetamine were packaged in a manner that is consistent with sale and distribution,” she said in the release.
Ramos-Vargas was charged with felony possession with intent to sell or deliver methamphetamine, felony possession with intent to sell or deliver marijuana, felony possession of a Schedule I controlled substance, felony maintaining a dwelling for a controlled substance and misdemeanor possession of drug paraphernalia.
A Nash County magistrate issued Ramos-Vargas a $5,000 secured bond and scheduled his first-appearance hearing for Thursday, May 21.
COMMUNITY ACTION TEAM
Frisbee announced the NCSO’s Community Action Team has been formed “to reduce and deter crime within Nash County.”
“The team’s primary focus is gathering information from the community and addressing citizen complaints related to illegal drugs, firearms, wanted subjects and other areas of concern that require law enforcement attention,” she said in the news release.
Deputies with the CAT investigated Ramos-Vargas after receiving a request from a citizen to investigate the alleged use and sale of illegal drugs at the Issette Lane home.
“This team is highly proactive and motivated to serve the community and help deter crime in areas of concern quickly and swiftly,” Frisbee said. “A quick action team such as this will help curb the intense problem with illegal drugs that leads to overdoses and deaths. The development of this team is an additional resource we can utilize to provide the customer service the citizens of Nash County deserve, and one more tool we have to fight against gangs, guns and drugs.”
